clips.title: Wrong supplier at receiving
clips.transcript: The associate compares the delivery note with carton labels and notices the supplier name does not match the expected delivery.
clips.description: A delivery arrives with a supplier mismatch. The learner must catch it before counting or inspection effort is spent.
clips.expectedObservation: Supplier identity on cartons does not match the delivery note or purchase order.
clips.expectedDecision: Reject or hold the delivery at the dock and notify the supervisor before unloading continues.
clips.lessonContent: A wrong-supplier delivery is caught at the earliest receiving step. Continuing to count or inspect the wrong shipment wastes effort and risks accepting stock that should never enter the dock flow.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What is the safest next action when supplier identity does not match?

answerOptions.label: Stop unloading, reject or hold, and escalate
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Supplier mismatch is a dock-level stop condition.

answerOptions.label: Continue counting first
answerOptions.feedback: Counting should not continue when the delivery identity itself is wrong.

answerOptions.label: Accept now and fix paperwork later
answerOptions.feedback: That creates a serious receiving control failure.

clips.title: Vendor FNV crate count check
clips.transcript: A vendor truck unloads FNV crates while receiving associates scan crate labels and count crates against the digital receiving task.
clips.description: Fresh fruits and vegetables are checked at the dock by crate label, count and basic item condition before moving to inspection.
clips.expectedObservation: Crate labels, counts and item condition must be checked before FNV crates enter the inspection flow.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan and count the crates against the digital receiving task before moving them forward.
clips.lessonContent: Vendor receiving is the first inventory control point. Crate count and label verification prevent shortages, wrong-item flow and untraceable produce before quality inspection starts.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should be checked before vendor FNV crates move to inspection?

answerOptions.label: Crate labels and count against the digital task
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. This confirms both identity and quantity before inspection.

answerOptions.label: Only whether the vegetables look fresh
answerOptions.feedback: Freshness matters, but it does not replace label and count verification.

answerOptions.label: Only the driver’s verbal confirmation
answerOptions.feedback: Driver confirmation is not a system-controlled receiving record.

clips.title: FNV crate receiving scan
clips.transcript: Fresh produce crates arrive at the receiving dock. The associate scans crate labels and verifies that the FNV delivery is ready for inspection flow.
clips.description: Fruits and vegetables are received in crates before they move to quality inspection or temperature-controlled staging.
clips.expectedObservation: FNV crates must be scanned and kept in the right receiving flow before inspection.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan crate identity and move the FNV shipment into the correct receiving-to-inspection lane.
clips.lessonContent: Fresh produce is high-volume and time-sensitive. Receiving associates must scan crate identity and maintain the correct FNV flow so quality teams can inspect without losing traceability.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the associate confirm before moving FNV crates forward?

answerOptions.label: Crate identity and correct FNV flow
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. FNV crates need traceable receiving before inspection.

answerOptions.label: Only the crate colour
answerOptions.feedback: Crate colour alone does not prove delivery identity or flow.

answerOptions.label: Skip scanning if crates look fresh
answerOptions.feedback: Fresh appearance does not replace receiving traceability.

clips.title: Frozen goods temperature check
clips.transcript: A refrigerated truck arrives. The receiving associate checks the frozen cartons with a temperature probe before accepting the shipment.
clips.description: A frozen-food delivery arrives for restaurant supply. The learner must notice that temperature is checked before acceptance.
clips.expectedObservation: Frozen goods must be temperature-checked before acceptance.
clips.expectedDecision: Hold acceptance until cold-chain condition is verified and escalate if outside limits.
clips.lessonContent: Frozen products can become unsafe if the cold chain is broken. The first receiving action is to verify temperature and condition before the cartons enter normal stock flow.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the associate check before accepting frozen goods?

answerOptions.label: Product temperature and cold-chain condition
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Temperature and cold-chain condition decide whether frozen goods can be accepted.

answerOptions.label: Carton colour
answerOptions.feedback: Carton colour is not the safety control. Temperature and condition come first.

answerOptions.label: Driver name
answerOptions.feedback: Driver identity may matter administratively, but it does not replace cold-chain verification.

clips.title: Bakery crate barcode scan
clips.transcript: The associate moves barcoded bread crates along the receiving conveyor, scanning each one before it continues down the line.
clips.description: Barcoded bakery crates arrive on the receiving conveyor. The learner must scan each crate individually rather than assuming visually identical crates match.
clips.expectedObservation: Each crate carries its own barcode label that must be scanned before it moves further down the line.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan every crate individually, even when several crates look identical.
clips.lessonContent: Skipping scans on visually identical crates is a common shortcut that lets mismatched or expired stock through undetected. Every crate gets its own scan, no exceptions.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Should the associate scan every crate, even if they look identical?

answerOptions.label: Yes, scan each crate individually
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- visually identical crates can still differ in batch or expiry.

answerOptions.label: No, one scan covers the batch
answerOptions.feedback: This risks letting mismatched or expired stock through unchecked.

clips.title: FNV damage segregation
clips.transcript: A quality associate checks tomatoes and leafy greens, finds visible damage, and moves one crate aside for quality hold.
clips.description: Fresh produce is inspected for visible spoilage, bruising, excess moisture, and freshness before acceptance.
clips.expectedObservation: One FNV crate has visible quality damage and should not flow into accepted stock.
clips.expectedDecision: Separate the damaged crate and record it for quality hold or supervisor review.
clips.lessonContent: FNV quality issues must be separated at inspection. Mixing damaged stock with accepted crates can affect restaurant order quality and food safety.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should be done with the damaged FNV crate?

answerOptions.label: Move it aside for quality hold
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Damaged produce should be segregated and recorded.

answerOptions.label: Mix it with accepted crates
answerOptions.feedback: Mixing damaged stock hides the issue and weakens quality control.

answerOptions.label: Ignore it if only one crate is affected
answerOptions.feedback: Small exceptions still need to be recorded and controlled.

clips.title: Egg tray damage check
clips.transcript: A quality associate checks incoming egg trays for cracked or broken eggs before the crate is accepted.
clips.description: Incoming egg trays are checked at receiving inspection. The learner must decide what to do when a tray has visibly cracked eggs.
clips.expectedObservation: One or more eggs in the tray are visibly cracked or broken.
clips.expectedDecision: Remove and segregate the damaged tray rather than accepting the full crate as-is.
clips.lessonContent: Cracked eggs are a food-safety risk and can also mark other product in the same crate. Damaged trays must be segregated at receiving, not passed downstream.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the associate do when a tray has cracked eggs?

answerOptions.label: Segregate the damaged tray
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- prevents a food-safety risk from moving downstream.

answerOptions.label: Accept the full crate as normal
answerOptions.feedback: Cracked eggs are a real safety and cross-contamination risk -- always segregate.

clips.title: Chilled dairy immediate put-away
clips.transcript: The associate scans dairy crates and moves them quickly from receiving into a chilled room instead of leaving them at ambient temperature.
clips.description: Chilled dairy products are transferred into cold storage without unnecessary dwell time.
clips.expectedObservation: Dairy stock should not remain in the ambient receiving area.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan and move dairy crates into chilled storage promptly.
clips.lessonContent: Chilled dairy has a narrow handling window. The correct process is to scan, verify, and move it to the chilled zone quickly while preserving traceability.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What is the priority after chilled dairy is verified?

answerOptions.label: Move it to chilled storage promptly
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Chilled dairy should not dwell at ambient temperature.

answerOptions.label: Leave it at the dock until all goods are received
answerOptions.feedback: That increases cold-chain risk.

answerOptions.label: Store it in ambient racks temporarily
answerOptions.feedback: Dairy must go to the correct chilled zone.

clips.title: Storing dairy crates in cold storage
clips.transcript: An associate carries stacked dairy crates into the cold room and stacks them while the chilled room door stands open.
clips.description: Dairy crates are stacked into cold storage. The learner must decide what to do about the open cold room door once the crates are in place.
clips.expectedObservation: The chilled room door stands open while crates are carried in and stacked.
clips.expectedDecision: Close the cold room door as soon as the crates are stacked, minimizing how long it stays open.
clips.lessonContent: Every extra second a chilled room door stays open raises the internal temperature for all stock inside, not just the crates being handled. Storage trips should be planned to minimize open-door time.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the associate do once the crates are stacked in the cold room?

answerOptions.label: Close the cold room door right away
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- minimizes temperature excursion for the rest of the chilled stock.

answerOptions.label: Leave it open for the next trip
answerOptions.feedback: This raises the temperature for all stock in the room -- always close between trips.

clips.title: Ambient staples location scan
clips.transcript: The associate scans a carton of staples, then scans the rack location label before placing it in the ambient storage bay.
clips.description: Ambient staples such as rice, flour, pulses, spices, and oil cans are placed only after product and location scans.
clips.expectedObservation: Both item barcode and rack location must be scanned to prevent inventory mismatch.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan product and location before completing put-away.
clips.lessonContent: Location accuracy matters as much as physical movement. A missed rack scan can make stock unavailable for restaurant orders even when it is physically present.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Which scans are required before put-away is completed?

answerOptions.label: Product barcode and rack location
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Both scans preserve inventory accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Product barcode only
answerOptions.feedback: Product-only scanning does not prove the item reached the right bin.

answerOptions.label: Rack location only
answerOptions.feedback: Location-only scanning does not prove which stock was placed.

clips.title: PPE check before entering the processing area
clips.transcript: Associates put on hairnets and aprons at the handwashing station before passing through the strip curtain into the processing area.
clips.description: Associates prepare to enter a food processing area through a strip-curtain doorway. The learner must decide when required PPE should go on.
clips.expectedObservation: Hairnets and aprons are already on before the associates step through the strip curtain.
clips.expectedDecision: Put on all required PPE at the entry station before entering, not after stepping inside.
clips.lessonContent: Food-processing PPE exists to keep contaminants out of the product area. Putting it on after entering defeats the purpose -- gowning and hairnets go on at the entry station, every time, before crossing the threshold.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should hairnets and aprons be put on?

answerOptions.label: At the entry station, before stepping inside
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- PPE only protects the processing area if it's on before you cross the threshold.

answerOptions.label: Just inside, once through the curtain
answerOptions.feedback: This lets contamination in during the gap -- PPE goes on before entry, not after.

clips.title: FNV paper bag packing
clips.transcript: Associates pack fresh vegetables from large crates into 500 gram and 1 kilogram paper bags while potatoes and onions are portioned from bulk sacks.
clips.description: Fresh vegetables move from bulk crates and sacks into customer-ready pack sizes using weighing and item verification.
clips.expectedObservation: Pack size, item identity, hygiene and weight must be controlled before the bag moves forward.
clips.expectedDecision: Verify item and weight on the scale before closing or staging the paper bag.
clips.lessonContent: FNV packing converts bulk inventory into ordered pack sizes. Associates must keep products separate, use clean handling and verify weight so customers receive the right quantity.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What must be confirmed before a packed vegetable bag goes to staging?

answerOptions.label: The item and weight match the order
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Pack-size accuracy is the main control.

answerOptions.label: Only that the bag looks full
answerOptions.feedback: Visual fullness does not prove 500g or 1kg accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Only that it came from the same table
answerOptions.feedback: The table location does not prove item or weight accuracy.

clips.title: MOQ crate preparation
clips.transcript: Workers prepare minimum-order-quantity crates by scanning the order, picking exact quantities, and moving the completed crate to staging.
clips.description: Restaurant, hotel, and cafe orders are prepared in customer-ready crates with item and quantity checks.
clips.expectedObservation: MOQ preparation must match the order quantity and customer crate identity.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan the order, verify item quantity, and stage only correctly prepared crates.
clips.lessonContent: MOQ preparation converts warehouse stock into customer-ready quantities. Associates must scan, count, and stage carefully so downstream dispatch does not inherit errors.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What must be verified before an MOQ crate goes to staging?

answerOptions.label: Item, quantity, and customer crate identity
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. All three protect order accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Only that the crate looks full
answerOptions.feedback: Visual fullness does not prove quantity or customer identity.

answerOptions.label: Skip verification during peak time
answerOptions.feedback: Peak load is when scan discipline matters most.

clips.title: Building a mixed-item ambient pallet
clips.transcript: Two associates stack staple sacks and cartons onto a single pallet for onward staging.
clips.description: A mixed pallet of ambient staples is being built. The learner must decide how to sequence heavy sacks against lighter cartons.
clips.expectedObservation: Heavier sacks are placed at the base of the pallet, lighter cartons on top.
clips.expectedDecision: Keep the heaviest items at the bottom of the stack to keep the pallet stable and avoid crushing lighter goods.
clips.lessonContent: A pallet built top-heavy, or with heavy sacks resting on cartons, is a tip and crush risk in transit. Always sequence the heaviest, most crush-resistant items at the base.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Where should the heaviest sacks go when building a mixed pallet?

answerOptions.label: At the base of the pallet
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- keeps the load stable and protects lighter items on top.

answerOptions.label: On top, for easy access
answerOptions.feedback: This risks crushing lighter cartons underneath and destabilizing the pallet.

clips.title: Staging vegetables for processing
clips.transcript: Associates move trolleys of produce from storage racks toward the processing tables, keeping to the marked aisle lane.
clips.description: Multiple associates stage vegetables from storage into the processing area using trolleys. The learner must decide how to move through a shared aisle safely.
clips.expectedObservation: Trolleys stay within the yellow lane markings on the floor as they move between the storage racks and the processing tables.
clips.expectedDecision: Keep trolleys within the marked lane so the aisle stays clear for cross traffic.
clips.lessonContent: Marked floor lanes exist so multiple associates can move produce through the same aisle without blocking each other or cross traffic. Straying outside the lane -- even briefly -- creates a collision risk in a busy processing floor.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Where should a trolley stay while moving produce through a shared aisle?

answerOptions.label: Within the marked yellow lane
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- keeps the aisle clear and predictable for everyone else moving through it.

answerOptions.label: Wherever is fastest at the time
answerOptions.feedback: This creates unpredictable collision risk for other associates and cross traffic.

clips.title: Verifying sack weight before sealing
clips.transcript: An associate places a produce sack on a digital scale and checks the reading before sealing it.
clips.description: A 50kg produce sack is weighed before sealing. The learner must decide when to confirm the weight against the target.
clips.expectedObservation: The digital scale display is checked while the sack sits on the platform, before it is sealed.
clips.expectedDecision: Confirm the scale reading matches the target weight before sealing the sack, not after.
clips.lessonContent: Sealing a sack before confirming its weight means any shortfall or overfill only gets caught later, if at all -- after it's harder to correct. The scale reading has to be checked while the sack is still open.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should the associate check the scale reading?

answerOptions.label: Before sealing the sack
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- lets a shortfall or overfill be corrected while the sack is still open.

answerOptions.label: After sealing, as a final check
answerOptions.feedback: By then the sack is harder to correct -- always confirm weight before sealing.

clips.title: Weighing and bagging produce for orders
clips.transcript: Associates portion carrots and cucumbers onto a scale before bagging them into paper bags for outbound orders.
clips.description: A team portions produce into bags at a bagging line. The learner must decide whether to rely on the scale or estimate quantities by eye.
clips.expectedObservation: Each portion is weighed on the scale before it goes into the bag.
clips.expectedDecision: Confirm the scale reading for every bag rather than estimating the quantity by eye.
clips.lessonContent: Eyeballing produce quantities to save time is a common shortcut that produces inconsistent bag weights -- some short, some over. Checking the scale for every bag is what keeps orders accurate and consistent.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Should each bag's quantity be estimated by eye or confirmed on the scale?

answerOptions.label: Confirmed on the scale every time
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- keeps bag weights consistent instead of drifting short or over.

answerOptions.label: Estimated by eye to save time
answerOptions.feedback: This produces inconsistent bag weights -- always confirm on the scale.

clips.title: Ambient staples SPR pick
clips.transcript: A picker scans a WMS task in the ambient SPR aisle, scans the rack location, selects the correct carton, and places it into an order crate.
clips.description: Ambient staples are picked from selective pallet racking using task, location, and item confirmation.
clips.expectedObservation: The picker follows the WMS-directed pick path and confirms the rack location before taking stock.
clips.expectedDecision: Pick only after task, location, item, and quantity match.
clips.lessonContent: Large ambient warehouses depend on location accuracy. Even when the item appears obvious, picking must follow task and rack confirmation to avoid restaurant order errors.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What is the correct picking control in the ambient SPR aisle?

answerOptions.label: Match task, location, item, and quantity
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. This prevents wrong-stock and wrong-quantity picks.

answerOptions.label: Pick the nearest similar case
answerOptions.feedback: Similar-looking cartons can create order errors.

answerOptions.label: Use memory instead of scanning
answerOptions.feedback: Memory is not a reliable WMS control.

clips.title: Frozen order item scan
clips.transcript: A picker scans a frozen pick task, verifies the rack location, selects the correct carton, and places it into the order crate.
clips.description: Frozen picking requires location scan discipline while preserving cold-chain handling.
clips.expectedObservation: The picker verifies both task and rack location before selecting frozen stock.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan the rack and item, pick the requested quantity, and keep the carton in the correct cold-chain flow.
clips.lessonContent: Frozen picking has two risks: wrong item selection and cold-chain exposure. The picker must follow the WMS task and scan the location before moving stock.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the picker scan before taking the frozen carton?

answerOptions.label: Task, rack location, and item
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. These scans prove the right frozen stock was picked.

answerOptions.label: Only the item barcode
answerOptions.feedback: Item-only scanning misses location discipline.

answerOptions.label: No scan if the carton is visible
answerOptions.feedback: Visual recognition is not enough for inventory control.

clips.title: Staying alert to forklift traffic while picking
clips.transcript: A forklift operates in the same tall-racking aisle an associate is walking through to pick items.
clips.description: A forklift shares the picking aisle with a pedestrian associate. The learner must decide how to behave when a forklift is operating nearby.
clips.expectedObservation: The forklift is active in the same aisle the associate needs to walk through.
clips.expectedDecision: Stay visible, make eye contact with the operator, and let the forklift complete its move before crossing its path.
clips.lessonContent: Forklifts have significant blind spots and stopping distance. A pedestrian who assumes the operator has seen them, or tries to slip past while the forklift is moving, is taking on real risk that's entirely avoidable by waiting.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the associate do when a forklift is active in the same aisle?

answerOptions.label: Stay visible and wait for the forklift to finish its move
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- forklifts have blind spots; never assume the operator has seen you.

answerOptions.label: Move past quickly while there's a gap
answerOptions.feedback: This risks a collision -- always wait for confirmed clearance, not just a gap.

clips.title: Stacking fragile items safely on the picking trolley
clips.transcript: Associates load egg trays and other fragile items onto a picking trolley alongside heavier boxes.
clips.description: A picking trolley is loaded with a mix of fragile egg trays and heavier boxes. The learner must decide how to stack them for the trip through the aisle.
clips.expectedObservation: Fragile egg trays are placed on top of the load, not underneath the heavier boxes.
clips.expectedDecision: Load fragile items on top of the stack, never underneath heavier boxes that could crush them in transit.
clips.lessonContent: A moving trolley shifts and jolts more than a stationary pallet. Fragile trays placed under heavier boxes have no protection from that movement -- they always go on top, where nothing can crush them.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Where should fragile egg trays go when loading a picking trolley with other items?

answerOptions.label: On top of the load
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- protects them from being crushed by heavier items during the trip.

answerOptions.label: Underneath, to save space on top
answerOptions.feedback: This risks crushing the fragile trays under heavier boxes -- always load fragile items on top.

clips.title: Order-level crate merge
clips.transcript: A dispatch associate scans crates from different temperature zones and groups them into the correct customer order staging lane.
clips.description: Crates from frozen, chilled, FNV, and ambient flows are merged at order level before route loading.
clips.expectedObservation: Each crate must belong to the same customer order before it is grouped for dispatch.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan every crate and hold mismatched crates outside the order staging lane.
clips.lessonContent: Order-level merge is where separate warehouse flows become one customer delivery. Scan discipline prevents a frozen, chilled, FNV, or ambient crate from joining the wrong order.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should dispatch verify during order-level merge?

answerOptions.label: All crates belong to the same customer order
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Dispatch merge protects customer-order accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Only that crate colours match
answerOptions.feedback: Crate colour does not prove customer order identity.

answerOptions.label: Load quickly without scanning
answerOptions.feedback: Skipping scan makes misdelivery more likely.

clips.title: Staging order completion check
clips.transcript: Ambient crates, frozen ice boxes, FNV crates, bread trays and egg cartons arrive at one staging lane where associates scan and check order completion before loading.
clips.description: Customer orders are accumulated across temperature zones and checked for completeness before vehicle loading starts.
clips.expectedObservation: All expected crates, totes, cartons and ice boxes must be scanned into the same order group before loading.
clips.expectedDecision: Do not load until the digital task shows the full order is complete.
clips.lessonContent: Dispatch staging is the final completeness check before loading. Missing one crate, carton or ice box can cause a customer shortage even if earlier picking was correct.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the team verify before loading this staged order?

answerOptions.label: The full order is scanned and complete
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Loading starts only after completion is confirmed.

answerOptions.label: Only that the vehicle has arrived
answerOptions.feedback: Vehicle arrival does not prove the order is complete.

answerOptions.label: Only that some crates are ready
answerOptions.feedback: Partial readiness is not enough for dispatch loading.

clips.title: Ambient small-vehicle crate loading
clips.transcript: Dispatch associates scan ambient totes, crates and cartons before loading them into a small Bolero-style delivery vehicle by route sequence.
clips.description: Ambient orders are loaded into a compact goods vehicle with scan control and route sequencing.
clips.expectedObservation: Each tote, crate and carton is scanned before it is placed into the assigned small vehicle.
clips.expectedDecision: Load only scanned crates for the route and arrange them securely in delivery sequence.
clips.lessonContent: Small vehicle loading still needs WMS discipline. Associates must scan every crate and load by route sequence so the driver can deliver without searching or mixing orders.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What is required before loading crates into the small ambient vehicle?

answerOptions.label: Scan each crate and load by route sequence
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. This protects route and customer accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Load whatever is nearest first
answerOptions.feedback: That can break route sequence and cause delivery delays.

answerOptions.label: Skip scans because it is a small vehicle
answerOptions.feedback: Vehicle size does not remove scan-control requirements.

clips.title: Loading perishable stock into a refrigerated vehicle
clips.transcript: Perishable crates are packed into insulated containers and loaded directly from the dock into a refrigerated truck.
clips.description: Perishable produce and chilled goods are staged at the dock in insulated containers before loading. The learner must decide how long that stock should wait at the dock.
clips.expectedObservation: Perishable stock is packed into insulated containers and moved straight from the dock into the refrigerated truck.
clips.expectedDecision: Load perishable stock into the refrigerated vehicle promptly rather than leaving it staged on the open dock.
clips.lessonContent: Every minute perishable stock spends staged on an open dock is time outside the cold chain, even inside insulated containers. Loading should happen as soon as the vehicle is ready, not whenever it's convenient.
clips.assessmentQuestion: How long should perishable stock wait at the dock before loading?

answerOptions.label: As little time as possible -- load as soon as the vehicle is ready
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- minimizes time outside the cold chain, even in insulated containers.

answerOptions.label: However long is convenient for the loading schedule
answerOptions.feedback: This extends time outside the cold chain -- perishables should move to the vehicle promptly.

clips.title: Verifying the load manifest before departure
clips.transcript: A supervisor checks a handheld device against the crates loaded onto a delivery vehicle before it departs.
clips.description: A supervisor coordinates with associates loading a delivery vehicle, checking a handheld device against what's been loaded. The learner must decide when this check should happen.
clips.expectedObservation: The supervisor checks the manifest on the handheld device while the vehicle is still at the dock, before it pulls away.
clips.expectedDecision: Confirm the loaded crates match the manifest before the vehicle departs, not after.
clips.lessonContent: A manifest mismatch caught after the vehicle has left the dock means a delayed correction, a return trip, or a customer receiving the wrong order. The check has to happen while the vehicle is still there to fix.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should the loaded crates be checked against the manifest?

answerOptions.label: Before the vehicle departs
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- any mismatch can still be corrected while the vehicle is at the dock.

answerOptions.label: After departure, if an issue comes up
answerOptions.feedback: By then correcting a mismatch means a delay or a return trip -- always verify before departure.

clips.title: Restaurant delivery handover
clips.transcript: The delivery associate unloads crates at a restaurant, scans the order, counts crates with the receiver, and completes digital handover.
clips.description: Delivery handover confirms that the correct crates reached the customer and were acknowledged digitally.
clips.expectedObservation: The associate counts crates with the receiver and records proof of delivery on the device.
clips.expectedDecision: Complete digital handover only after crate count and customer acknowledgement match.
clips.lessonContent: The last control point is customer handover. A clean scan, count, and acknowledgement protects both the warehouse and the customer from disputed deliveries.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should digital handover be completed?

answerOptions.label: After crate count and customer acknowledgement match
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Proof of delivery needs both count and acknowledgement.

answerOptions.label: Before unloading starts
answerOptions.feedback: The receiver must confirm actual delivered crates.

answerOptions.label: Without customer acknowledgement
answerOptions.feedback: That weakens proof of delivery.

clips.title: Driver empty-crate and cash settlement
clips.transcript: A driver returns after deliveries with empty crates, totes, ice boxes and a cash pouch. Staff count assets, scan returns and receive the collection at the counter.
clips.description: Post-route settlement reconciles physical returnable assets and cash collection before the route is closed.
clips.expectedObservation: Empty crates, totes, ice boxes and cash must be counted, scanned and submitted at the settlement counter.
clips.expectedDecision: Reconcile returned assets and collections before closing the delivery route.
clips.lessonContent: A route is not complete when the delivery vehicle returns. Empty crates, totes, ice boxes and collections must be reconciled so asset losses and cash exceptions are visible.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What must happen before the driver route is closed?

answerOptions.label: Reconcile returned assets and cash collection
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Both asset and collection settlement are route-close controls.

answerOptions.label: Only park the vehicle at the dock
answerOptions.feedback: Parking the vehicle does not close the route.

answerOptions.label: Count empty crates later without the driver
answerOptions.feedback: Delayed counting weakens accountability for returnable assets.

clips.title: Returned goods quarantine
clips.transcript: A returned carton from a restaurant delivery is placed in a quarantine area while the supervisor checks the return reason and condition.
clips.description: Returned food-service goods are separated from saleable stock until disposition is approved.
clips.expectedObservation: Returned goods must not be mixed back into available inventory without review.
clips.expectedDecision: Move returns to quarantine and wait for supervisor disposition.
clips.lessonContent: Returns may have unknown handling history. Quarantine protects customers and inventory accuracy until the approved disposition is recorded.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Where should returned goods go before approval?

answerOptions.label: Quarantine area
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Returned goods require controlled review before disposition.

answerOptions.label: Available stock rack
answerOptions.feedback: Returned goods cannot be mixed into available stock without review.

answerOptions.label: Nearest empty space
answerOptions.feedback: Returns need controlled quarantine, not convenience storage.

clips.title: General carton damage check while unloading
clips.transcript: Associates unload cartons from a delivery truck onto the receiving conveyor, checking each one as it comes off.
clips.description: Cartons are unloaded from a truck onto the receiving conveyor. The learner must decide when to check each carton for damage.
clips.expectedObservation: Each carton is visually checked for damage as it's placed on the conveyor, not after it has already moved on.
clips.expectedDecision: Check each carton for damage at the point of unloading, before it moves further down the line.
clips.lessonContent: A damaged carton caught at unloading can be set aside immediately. The same carton caught further down the line means retracing where it came from and which other cartons might share the same issue.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should a carton be checked for damage?

answerOptions.label: At the point of unloading, before it moves on
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- catches the issue immediately, before it's mixed in with other stock.

answerOptions.label: Later, whenever there's time
answerOptions.feedback: This risks damaged stock moving further into the flow before anyone notices.

clips.title: Supervisor quality check on packed produce bags
clips.transcript: A supervisor moves between associates packing produce into paper bags, checking the packed bags as they're completed.
clips.description: A supervisor oversees a team packing produce into bags. The learner must decide how the supervisor should verify packing quality.
clips.expectedObservation: The supervisor checks completed bags against the associates, rather than only observing from a distance.
clips.expectedDecision: Spot-check completed bags directly rather than relying on visual observation of the packing process alone.
clips.lessonContent: Watching associates work looks productive but doesn't catch a badly packed bag that looked fine from a distance. A supervisor's oversight role means directly checking finished output, not just monitoring activity.
clips.assessmentQuestion: How should a supervisor verify packing quality?

answerOptions.label: Spot-check completed bags directly
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- directly verifying finished output catches issues that observation alone would miss.

answerOptions.label: Observe the packing process from a distance
answerOptions.feedback: This can miss quality issues in the finished bags themselves -- direct checks are needed.

clips.title: Handling a missing item found during sortation
clips.transcript: Associates work along a long sortation line of crates and insulated containers, checking labels against what should be in each order.
clips.description: Orders move along a sortation line where associates verify contents against labels. The learner must decide what to do when an item appears to be missing from an order.
clips.expectedObservation: Associates check each container's contents against its label as it moves along the sortation line.
clips.expectedDecision: Flag the order with the missing item and escalate it rather than letting it continue to dispatch incomplete.
clips.lessonContent: An order that dispatches with a missing item becomes a customer-facing problem instead of a warehouse-facing one. Catching it on the sortation line and escalating it is far cheaper than a return or a complaint after delivery.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should happen when an item appears to be missing from an order on the sortation line?

answerOptions.label: Flag the order and escalate before it continues
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- catches the issue before it becomes a customer-facing problem.

answerOptions.label: Let it continue and note it for later
answerOptions.feedback: This lets an incomplete order reach the customer -- flag and escalate immediately instead.

clips.title: Checking dock and vehicle temperature before frozen loading
clips.transcript: Two associates at a frozen dock bay check a probe thermometer reading on the reefer vehicle before any crates are loaded.
clips.description: A refrigerated vehicle is backed into a frozen dock bay. The learner must decide when the vehicle's temperature should be verified relative to loading.
clips.expectedObservation: Associates check the vehicle's internal temperature with a probe thermometer before any crates are loaded.
clips.expectedDecision: Confirm the vehicle has reached the correct frozen temperature before loading begins, not after.
clips.lessonContent: Loading frozen stock into a vehicle that hasn't reached temperature defeats the purpose of the cold chain before the trip even starts. The check has to happen before the first crate goes in, not once loading is already underway.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should the vehicle's temperature be checked before loading frozen stock?

answerOptions.label: Before any crates are loaded
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- loading into a vehicle that hasn't reached temperature defeats the cold chain before the trip starts.

answerOptions.label: Partway through loading, once a few crates are in
answerOptions.feedback: By then some stock has already gone into a vehicle that wasn't ready -- check before loading starts.

clips.title: Sealing a refrigerated vehicle after loading
clips.transcript: After loading a refrigerated vehicle, an associate scans a tamper-evident seal on a handheld device, confirmed by a "seal secured" message.
clips.description: A refrigerated vehicle has just finished loading. The learner must decide when the vehicle's security seal should be applied and confirmed.
clips.expectedObservation: The associate applies and scans a tamper-evident seal on the vehicle immediately after loading is complete, confirmed on the handheld device.
clips.expectedDecision: Apply and confirm the security seal right after loading finishes, before the vehicle leaves the dock.
clips.lessonContent: A loaded vehicle without a confirmed seal has no proof its contents weren't tampered with between the dock and the customer. Sealing and confirming it on the device right after loading closes that gap before the vehicle ever moves.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should a vehicle's security seal be applied and confirmed?

answerOptions.label: Right after loading finishes, before the vehicle leaves
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- closes the tamper-evidence gap before the vehicle moves.

answerOptions.label: Whenever convenient before the next trip
answerOptions.feedback: This leaves the vehicle unsealed and unverified in the meantime -- seal it right after loading.

clips.title: Confirming driver route assignments before departure
clips.transcript: A supervisor briefs a group of drivers on their route assignments against a whiteboard and a tablet, next to a line of staged delivery vehicles.
clips.description: Drivers gather near their staged vehicles before departure. The learner must decide when each driver's route assignment should be confirmed.
clips.expectedObservation: The supervisor confirms each driver's route assignment against the board and tablet before the driver takes their vehicle out.
clips.expectedDecision: Confirm each driver's route assignment before departure, rather than letting drivers leave without a final check against the assignment board.
clips.lessonContent: A driver who departs on the wrong route wastes the trip and delays every stop on both routes. A quick confirmation against the assignment board before the vehicle leaves catches a mix-up while it's still cheap to fix.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should a driver's route assignment be confirmed?

answerOptions.label: Before the driver departs with the vehicle
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- catches a mix-up while it's still easy to fix.

answerOptions.label: After departure, if a stop seems wrong
answerOptions.feedback: By then the driver is already on the wrong route -- confirm before departure instead.

clips.title: Verifying product temperature at restaurant handover
clips.transcript: At a restaurant delivery point, an associate probes a milk pouch with a thermometer before handing the crate over to kitchen staff.
clips.description: A delivery associate has arrived at a restaurant with chilled stock. The learner must decide when product temperature should be verified relative to handover.
clips.expectedObservation: The delivery associate checks the product temperature with a probe thermometer at the point of handover, before the restaurant accepts the delivery.
clips.expectedDecision: Verify the product temperature at the handover point before completing the delivery, not skip straight to handover.
clips.lessonContent: The cold chain isn't complete until the product is confirmed to still be at the right temperature when it reaches the customer. A quick probe check at handover catches a cold-chain breach before it becomes the restaurant's problem.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should product temperature be verified during a chilled delivery?

answerOptions.label: At the point of handover, before the restaurant accepts it
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- confirms the cold chain held all the way to the customer.

answerOptions.label: Skip it -- the vehicle was refrigerated, so it should be fine
answerOptions.feedback: A refrigerated vehicle doesn't guarantee the product itself held temperature -- always verify at handover.

clips.title: Resolving a shortage dispute at delivery
clips.transcript: A restaurant staff member points at a crate, questioning the delivered quantity. Both the delivery associate and the staff member check their own handheld devices.
clips.description: A restaurant raises a shortage claim as a delivery is being unloaded. The learner must decide how the delivery associate should respond.
clips.expectedObservation: Both the delivery associate and the restaurant staff check their own device records against what was physically delivered.
clips.expectedDecision: Verify the shortage against the system record on the handheld device before agreeing to any adjustment, rather than taking the claim at face value or dismissing it outright.
clips.lessonContent: A shortage claim at the door can be genuine or a miscount on either side. Checking the device record against what's physically there settles it accurately instead of the delivery associate having to just accept or reject the customer's word.
clips.assessmentQuestion: How should a delivery associate respond to a shortage claim at handover?

answerOptions.label: Check the device record against what was actually delivered
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- settles the dispute with the actual record instead of guesswork.

answerOptions.label: Accept the customer's claim without checking
answerOptions.feedback: This risks incorrect adjustments -- always verify against the device record first.

clips.title: Reconciling returned crates during dock intake
clips.transcript: Associates unload a returns truck, stacking crates by type, while a handheld on a stand nearby shows a route status screen.
clips.description: A returns vehicle is being unloaded at the dock. The learner must decide when the returned crate count should be reconciled against the system record.
clips.expectedObservation: Associates check the returned crate count against the route's system record as crates are unloaded, not just stack them and move on.
clips.expectedDecision: Reconcile the returned crate count against the system record as part of unloading, before the return route is marked closed.
clips.lessonContent: A route can only be closed out accurately once what actually came back matches what the system expects. Counting and reconciling crates while unloading catches a mismatch immediately, instead of discovering it after the route's already been closed.
clips.assessmentQuestion: When should returned crates be reconciled against the system record?

answerOptions.label: While unloading, before the route is marked closed
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- catches a mismatch before the route is signed off as complete.

answerOptions.label: After the route is already closed, if something seems off
answerOptions.feedback: This means the route was closed on unverified numbers -- reconcile during unloading instead.

clips.title: Resolving a flagged settlement exception before route closure
clips.transcript: A driver's handheld shows an exception flagged on the settlement screen. A supervisor points it out and works through it with the driver directly.
clips.description: A driver's settlement has an unresolved exception flagged on the device. The learner must decide what the supervisor should do about it.
clips.expectedObservation: The supervisor identifies the exception flagged on the driver's settlement screen and resolves it with the driver directly, rather than letting it sit in the pending queue.
clips.expectedDecision: Resolve a flagged settlement exception with the driver before the route is closed out, not leave it in the pending queue for later.
clips.lessonContent: An exception left in the pending queue means a route that should be closed stays open, and the underlying discrepancy doesn't get answered. Working it through with the driver on the spot closes both the exception and the route cleanly.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should happen when a driver's settlement shows a flagged exception?

answerOptions.label: Resolve it with the driver before closing the route
answerOptions.feedback: Correct -- closes both the exception and the route cleanly.

answerOptions.label: Leave it in the pending queue for later
answerOptions.feedback: This leaves the route open and the discrepancy unanswered -- resolve it with the driver on the spot.
